jobs.title: Regional Home Care Coordinator
jobs.description:
myPlace Health is built around a simple but powerful belief: older adults deserve the support they need to live safely, independently, and with dignity in their own communities. As a PACE (Program of All Inclusive Care for the Elderly) organization backed by SCAN Group, myPlace Health brings together customized medical care, social activities, and daily support for participants and their families – all under one roof.

Our centers are more than healthcare facilities. They are vibrant community hubs where participants are known by name, valued, and supported as whole people. Behind that experience is a dedicated, interdisciplinary team working together to coordinate care, remove barriers, and improve quality of life for some of the most medically and socially complex populations.

For employees, myPlace Health offers the opportunity to do deeply meaningful work in a highly collaborative setting. Team members are encouraged to contribute innovative ideas, and grow alongside a mission that prioritizes compassion, respect, and impact. The result is a culture where people feel connected—to their colleagues, their participants, and the communities they serve.

At myPlace Health, work is more than a job. It’s a shared commitment to honoring what matters most.

The Regional Home Care Coordinator is responsible for coordinating home care services and related support for participants to ensure services are delivered safely, effectively, and in alignment with each individualized plan of care. As a member of the Interdisciplinary Team, this role completes home-based assessments, supports care planning, monitors service delivery, coordinates with contracted providers and community-based resources, and provides nursing care within the Licensed Vocational Nurse scope of practice as needed.

The role also supports participant and caregiver education, documentation, quality oversight, and day-to-day coordination of home care services, durable medical equipment, and related needs. This regional position requires regular travel to participant homes and work from the PACE center to support care coordination, documentation, and administrative responsibilities across assigned sites.

Responsibilities

Coordinate home care services through contracted agencies to ensure services are delivered in accordance with each participant’s individualized plan of care, authorized service needs, and program standards.
Participate as an active member of the Interdisciplinary Team by completing home assessments, reassessments, change-of-condition evaluations, care planning activities, and ongoing review of participant home care needs.
Provide nursing care within the Licensed Vocational Nurse scope of practice, including wellness checks, medication administration, wound care, and other assigned clinical services in the home, clinic, and day center as needed.
Monitor participant condition and home care service delivery through collaboration with home care staff and external agencies, and report changes in condition, treatment concerns, or adverse reactions to the Registered Nurse, Physician, or other appropriate team members.
Educate participants and caregivers on in-home care needs, safety practices, and self-management strategies to promote participant independence, well-being, and continuity of care.
Respond to participant and family questions or concerns related to home care services in a timely, professional, and service-oriented manner.
Schedule and coordinate home care visits and support related appointment logistics, including collaboration with transportation staff to ensure timely and accurate participant service coordination.
Oversee and monitor services provided by contracted home care agencies to support quality, consistency, and compliance with applicable regulatory and organizational requirements.
Document all nursing care, care coordination, assessments, and service-related activities in the electronic medical record within established timeframes to ensure accuracy, continuity, and regulatory compliance.
Support home care operations and team effectiveness by participating in care coordination meetings, updating care plans as needed, and assisting with the training and orientation of new home care staff.
We seek Rebels who are curious about AI and its power to transform how we operate and serve our members.
Actively support the achievement of myPlace's Vision and Goals.
Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications & Experience

Current, active Licensed Vocational Nurse (LVN) license in the State of California
CPR and First Aid certification required within 60 days of hire
Experience providing care to frail and elderly adults
Travel 50% of the time covering both Downtown Los Angeles & Compton locations
Valid California driver’s license, insurance and reliable personal transportation
Strong verbal, written, and organizational skills
Ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary team environment
Proficiency in computer applications, typing, and electronic medical record systems
Ability to maintain professionalism, exercise sound judgment, and respond effectively under pressure
Demonstrated dependability, flexibility, and commitment to quality and ethical standards
Compassion, patience, and respect in working with older adults and their families
Prior experience in home care or community-based care settings preferred

Tuberculosis Screening Policy

To ensure the health and safety of our members, if you are selected for this position, your job offer with SCAN will be contingent on providing proof of Tuberculosis screening upon hire or providing proof of a negative screening within the last year. If you have a disability/medical reason or sincerely held religious belief that prevents you to provide information required in this policy, SCAN will initiate and engage in the interactive process to evaluate what, if any, reasonable accommodations may be available.

Base salary range: $27.01 - $39.40 per hour

Work Mode: Onsite

An annual employee bonus program

Medical, Dental, Vision coverage

Founded in 1965, UC Irvine
is a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities and is ranked among the nation’s top 10 public universities by U.S. News & World Report. To learn more about UC Irvine, visit www.uci.edu.

At NVIDIA, we redefine what’s possible in digital imaging, personal computer gaming, and high-performance computing. Now, we lead the charge into AI’s unlimited potential. Our GPUs act as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars. They enable these machines to understand and interact with the world in new ways. This is your chance to join a legacy of innovation and excellence. Work with the world’s best talent in a diverse and encouraging environment. Join us and make a lasting impact on the world!

This is an ambitious opportunity to work at the forefront of AI safety and contribute to groundbreaking advancements in technology.

What You’ll Be Doing

Lead cross-functional planning and execution for evaluation identification, selection and execution. With a focus on agentic-safety evaluations, including multi-turn tool calling, unsafe tool use, unintended actions, excessive autonomy, and multi-step failures.
Track execution, results for all evals, analysis, and the mitigation and research plans for improvement that will stem from results analysis. Translate evaluation findings into prioritized mitigation plans with accountable owners, committed dates, and measurable closure criteria
Lead end-to-end safety planning and execution for Nemotron models, including program scope, dependencies, risks, resources, and release-readiness criteria.
Translate technical safety priorities into executable programs covering LLM security, frontier risks, agentic safety, hallucinations
Establish and track multi-turn, multi-modal, multi-lingual, long-context, and reasoning model evaluations across relevant use cases, domains, languages, modalities, and model releases.
Establish governance for reviewing safety findings, assigning severity, determining release impact, and escalating unresolved risks. Ensure required safety evidence, approvals, exceptions, and risk-acceptance decisions are documented before release. Identify program gaps and critical dependencies early and drive decisions, escalations, recovery plans, and corrective actions.
Build (with AI for Code/AI for Work) and maintain dashboards and executive reporting for evaluation coverage, critical findings, mitigation progress, residual risk, and release readiness.

What We Need To See

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in computer science, engineering, data science, or a related technical field.
10+ years of experience in technical program management, engineering, product development, technical operations, or a similar area.
Strong understanding of LLM architecture, frameworks (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, Hugging Face), and model evaluation.
Familiarity with LLM development, post-training, inference, tool calling, evaluation datasets, and model-release lifecycles.
Experience directing programs related to AI/ML development, model evaluation, agentic safety, security, content safety, hallucinations, and/or production releases.
Familiarity with AI safety risks such as hallucinations, timely injection attacks, unsafe tool use, data poisoning, model manipulation, and unintended agent behavior.
Experience supporting model-safety evaluations, Red Teaming, adversarial testing, security assessments, or responsible-AI programs.
Ability to interpret technical evaluation findings and communicate their product, schedule, and release implications to leadership.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Experience with LLM Agentic Safety, Security, Red Teaming, Hallucinations, adversarial assessment, or Responsible AI.
Experience defining evaluation datasets, rubrics, benchmarks, and release gates.
Ability to use evaluation results and data to make clear release recommendations and communicate residual risk to leadership.
Experience crafting or operationalizing multi-turn, hallucination, adversarial, or agentic-safety evaluations.

Position Overview

SCOPE OF ROLE
:

The Rapid Re-Housing Support Specialist plays a key direct service role in the S:US Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF) program. They support veteran families’ housing goals and their access to core supportive services, including housing planning, income and benefits maximization, legal aid, and deliver support with permanent housing applications, temporary financial assistance and specialized services. The RRH Specialist supports veteran families’ housing search, placement and stabilization in their apartments. The RRH Specialist will provide day-to-day support to veteran households, and assist with outreach, engagement and service delivery to veteran participants across the five boroughs of NYC and Long Island. The RRH Specialist will work directly with stakeholders and veterans to enroll and support access to SSVF services and Temporary Financial Assistance. They manage the program’s service delivery to veteran households referred directly by local VA Medical Centers’ HUD VASH programs.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

Assist participants in the SSVF program to define, plan and achieve their goals related to SSVF such as homeless prevention/rapid rehousing, income and benefits maximization and other goals for their housing stability.
Meet with designated VA staff to review cases and enroll veterans referred by HUD VASH for SSVF Temporary Financial Assistance.
Collect, review and process all required paperwork to screen, enroll and serve Veterans with HUD VASH in the SSVF program.
Act as a close liaison between S:US and the local VA teams.
Process SSVF Temporary Financial Assistance and other services according to agency and VA standards.
Monitor and report on SSVF data as directed by program management.
Maintain a caseload of specialized SSVF cases, mostly comprised of HUD VASH referrals for TFA into the program.

- Organize and conduct structured group and individual activities that address client’s goals for housing.
- Provide specialized housing services to other staff members through clinical team meetings and individual conferences.
- Complete required documentation including, but not limited to housing plans, and clinical records.
- Participate in the Individual Treatment Planning process by assisting with client goal formulation, monitoring, and progress reporting.
- Perform direct service interventions as indicated in the ITP, and in coordination with other members of the treatment team.
- Assist in developing annual service goals and measuring and reporting progress.
- Identify the needs and sources(s) for housing resource materials and procure per Agency procedures.
- Establish and maintain communication and working relationships with other providers and leaders in the field to help assure housing resource availability and enhance the Agency’s working knowledge of housing issues.
- Obtain and document results of housing inspections for clients.

jobs.title: Community Engagement Coordinator
jobs.description:
Community Engagement Coordinator

Company Description

Habitat for Humanity Mid-Yellowstone Valley is part of a global nonprofit organization dedicated to building strength, stability, and self-reliance through shelter. Our affiliate brings together homeowners, volunteers, donors, businesses, faith communities, and community partners to create affordable housing solutions and stronger neighborhoods throughout the Mid-Yellowstone Valley.

Volunteers are at the heart of Habitat’s mission. Whether swinging a hammer on a construction site, helping at a community event, or supporting another area of the organization, volunteers make our work possible. Every member of our team plays a role in creating a welcoming, meaningful, and mission-centered experience for the people who give their time to Habitat.

Role Description

The Community Engagement Coordinator is a full-time, on-site position based in Billings, Montana. This highly people-focused role serves as a primary connection between Habitat for Humanity Mid-Yellowstone Valley and the volunteers, organizations, businesses, and community members who help advance our mission.

A significant focus of this position is volunteer recruitment, coordination, engagement, and stewardship. The Coordinator works to ensure volunteers have a positive experience from their first inquiry through their day of service and beyond. This includes recruiting individual and group volunteers, coordinating schedules and opportunities, communicating expectations, welcoming volunteers, supporting them while they serve, and helping build long-term relationships that encourage continued involvement with Habitat.

This is not strictly a desk-based outreach position. The Community Engagement Coordinator must be comfortable working alongside volunteers in a variety of environments, including active residential construction sites. The Coordinator may assist with volunteer check-in, orientation, site preparation, hospitality, safety communication, and general volunteer support throughout the build day.

Additional responsibilities include developing relationships with community organizations, businesses, faith communities, schools, civic groups, and other partners; coordinating community events and informational sessions; representing Habitat at public events and meetings; and supporting communication efforts through newsletters, social media, outreach campaigns, and other materials.

The Coordinator will also maintain volunteer and community engagement records, track participation and engagement metrics, gather feedback, and collaborate closely with Habitat's construction, development, ReStore, and leadership teams to connect community members with meaningful opportunities to participate in Habitat's mission.

Key Responsibilities

- Recruit and engage individual volunteers, corporate teams, faith communities, civic organizations, schools, and other community groups.
- Coordinate volunteer inquiries, registration, scheduling, confirmations, reminders, and follow-up communication.
- Welcome, orient, and support volunteers to create a safe, organized, inclusive, and meaningful service experience.
- Maintain regular communication with volunteers and develop strategies to encourage volunteer retention and continued engagement.
- Work directly with construction staff to coordinate volunteer needs and schedules for Habitat build sites.
- Be present on active construction sites to assist with volunteer check-in, orientation, hospitality, communication, and day-of support.
- Develop a basic understanding of Habitat construction activities in order to effectively communicate with and serve volunteers.
- Build and maintain relationships with community organizations, businesses, faith communities, schools, residents, and other partners.
- Plan and coordinate community outreach activities, volunteer events, informational sessions, and special events.
- Represent Habitat for Humanity Mid-Yellowstone Valley at community meetings, presentations, volunteer fairs, and public events.
- Develop and coordinate outreach communications, including newsletters, social media content, volunteer communications, and promotional materials.
- Maintain accurate volunteer and community engagement records and contact databases.
- Track volunteer participation, outreach activities, and other engagement metrics to help evaluate and strengthen community engagement efforts.
- Gather feedback from volunteers and community partners and identify opportunities to improve the volunteer experience.
- Collaborate across Habitat departments to connect volunteers and community partners with opportunities that best match organizational needs.
- Perform other mission-related duties as needed in support of Habitat's programs, events, and community initiatives.

Qualifications

- Demonstrated experience in volunteer management, volunteer recruitment, community engagement, community outreach, customer service, or relationship-based work.
- Strong interpersonal skills and a genuine ability to make volunteers and community members feel welcomed, valued, informed, and appreciated.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including public speaking, group facilitation, and active listening.
- Experience coordinating volunteers, events, schedules, logistics, or community activities.
- Ability to build and maintain relationships with people from diverse backgrounds, organizations, and sectors of the community.
- Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple projects, schedules, and priorities.
- Ability to work collaboratively as part of a team while also independently managing assigned responsibilities.
- Comfort using basic office software, databases, email communication, and social media platforms.
- Previous nonprofit, volunteer management, community development, construction, social services, hospitality, or related experience is preferred.
- High school diploma or equivalent required; post-secondary education in nonprofit management, communications, social work, community development, volunteer administration, or a related field is an asset.

Physical and Work Environment Requirements

This position includes work in an office environment, throughout the community, at special events, and on active residential construction sites.

Candidates must be willing and able to:

- Work outdoors in varying weather conditions.
- Navigate active construction sites, including uneven terrain and unfinished structures.
- Stand and walk for extended periods during volunteer builds and events.
- Occasionally lift, carry, or move supplies and materials associated with volunteer activities and events.
- Wear required personal protective equipment and follow all Habitat construction-site safety procedures.
- Work occasional evenings or weekends to support volunteer builds, community events, and organizational activities.
- Travel locally throughout the Mid-Yellowstone Valley, with reliable transportation for outreach and volunteer activities.

Construction experience is not required. A willingness to learn, participate, serve others, and be comfortable in a hands-on environment is.

What Success Looks Like

The successful Community Engagement Coordinator understands that volunteer management is more than filling available shifts. It is about building relationships.

Volunteers should leave a Habitat experience knowing their time mattered, understanding the impact they helped create, and wanting to come back. This position helps create that experience while building a stronger network of people and organizations invested in Habitat's mission and the communities we serve.

jobs.description:
Description

Positive Impact Health Centers (PIHC)
is a community leader in providing HIV prevention, care and treatment services. The PIHC model of care assures that persons with HIV have access to medical, pharmacy, dental, behavioral health and social services, providing the best opportunity for patients to achieve high-quality health outcomes.

JOB SUMMARY:
The Medical Case Manager (MCM) will provide medical case management services to eligible adult clinic patients at Positive Impact Health Centers, following applicable funding guidelines and best practice care models. The MCM will function as an integral member of an interdisciplinary team which may include the following: medical provider, behavioral health clinician, medication access specialist, clinical pharmacist, and supportive services staff (Community Health Worker, Patient Navigator, Retention/Adherence Manager).

This position description should not be interpreted as all-inclusive. It is intended to identify the major responsibilities and requirements of this position. The incumbent may be requested to perform job-related responsibilities and tasks other than those stated in this position description.

Essential Functions

Duties and Responsibilities:

Learn and remain current on practice issues related to HIV/AIDS, related medical diagnoses, and medical case management.
Provide medical case management services to identified patients of the clinic program, following medical case management guidelines established by HRSA/Ryan White and the Metropolitan Atlanta HIV Health Services Planning Council.
Complete biopsychosocial assessments with new and returning patients, utilizing required screening tools established by the Metropolitan Atlanta HIV Health Services Planning Council and Ryan White/HRSA.
Provide medical case management services to an average caseload size of 70 patients: develop a comprehensive Individualized Service Plan (ISP); provide ongoing monitoring of ISP with each patient to assess the efficacy of the plan; coordinate services to meet goals of the service plan.
Perform periodic re-evaluations and revisions/adaptations of service plans.
Provide adherence and retention counseling to ensure patients maintain health care.
Identify gaps in core and supportive services, including care resources, mental health, substance abuse, housing, nutrition, and transportation
Coordinate referrals and follow-up for medical and non-medical services.
Actively participate as part of an interdisciplinary care team to assess patient care needs and coordinate service referrals.
Assist patients with applications and ongoing eligibility for medication access programs (i.e. ADAP and pharmaceutical assistance programs), as needed to support clinic staff.
Assist Self-Managed patients with social service questions and related needs.
Develop network of additional community resources.
Document patient information, activities, referrals and consultations in a timely and accurate manner, through the use of the agency’s electronic medical record system and related reporting software.
Abide by all state, federal laws and agency policies as related to confidentiality and Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).
Assist the agency administration in the development of long-range plans, including goals and objectives, as directed by supervisor.
Abides by all agency policies and procedures, including conflict of interest policy.
Additional duties as assigned.

Requirements

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

Strong social work, nursing, or case management skills, including the ability to obtain a comprehensive psychosocial assessment and assist adult clients with the development of an individualized service plan;
Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to communicate effectively in a multi-cultural setting including target populations, volunteers, agency staff, and agency Board members;
Proficient computer skills for word processing, data entry, documentation, and navigation of Internet;
Comprehensive and up-to-date knowledge of HIV medical and case management fundamentals preferred;
Ability to adapt work style to accommodate both solitary and collaborative tasks;
Ability to function independently without close supervision;
Excellent time management techniques;
Consistent follow-through to completion of assigned tasks

Minimum Qualifications

Join Our Team as a Foster Care Coordinator!

Childhelp Tennessee’s Foster Family Services program is seeking a full-time Care Coordinator for our Knoxville office location. Please consider joining our team as we make a positive difference in the lives of foster children and their families in East TN!

Childhelp provides therapeutic foster home services to children in state custody as well as services to their families in the hope that we can achieve permanency for these children by safely reuniting them with their birth families, or providing these children with a permanent adoptive family if reunification is not possible.

As a Care Coordinator for Childhelp’s Foster Family Services program, you will work closely with our children in care, their biological parents, Childhelp therapeutic foster parents and other involved stakeholders- DCS workers, court staff, attorneys, therapists and others- to help these children and families reach their goals and achieve permanency. Childhelp Care Coordinators help ensure that the children and the families we serve receive all of the services they need- safe, loving and structured foster home environments, health services, therapeutic services if/as needed (counseling, OT, PT, speech, etc….), education services and others. Besides serving as a “case manager”, our Care Coordinators serve as active therapeutic mentors and teachers for ALL of our clients, provide crisis intervention when/as needed and advocate for the best interest of the children and families we serve.

What You'll Do

Making regular, timely home visits to our foster homes to check on the children and foster families to ensure that everyone is doing well and getting their needs met in an excellent way
Engaging, teaching and encouraging birth parents to complete the Permanency Plan goal in an effort to safely reunite children and families whenever possible
Providing crisis intervention to children as needed
Serving as part of the child and family’s Treatment Team and attend all case planning and progress meetings for the child and family (via court hearings, Child and Family Team Meetings, etc…)
Supervising therapeutic child and family visits
Assisting in Independent Living skills planning and training for children ages 14 and up
Documenting all contacts with the children and their families and as well as all the services they are currently receiving
Creating and implementing Treatment Plan and goals for the children we serve in our foster care program
Assisting our foster parents in obtaining and scheduling needed services for the child(ren) in their care
Providing and/or displaying excellent customer service, organizational and communication (verbal and written) skills
The ability to be creative, innovative, flexible and solution-focused in a fast-paced environment
The ability to be a supportive, encouraging member of the staff team and treatment team

Qualifications

Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Psychology, Counseling or a closely-related field is required
Minimum of 21 years of age
Ability to pass extensive background checks and pre-employment screenings
Possess a valid unrestricted driver’s license

Brief Description

Are you ready to make a real difference in people's lives? Join the Harris Center for Mental Health and IDD as a Care Coordinator
. Under the general direction of the Clinical Team Lead, Care Coordinator (CC) provides case management and coordination of care services. The Care Coordinator will provide all services within the community for individuals participating in a housing program affiliated with the Coalition for the Homeless. The CC will provide care coordination and case management services as part of a multidisciplinary team that includes a Master Level Clinician or LPHA and LCDC. Peer support services are also offered within the program. The CC will be expected to provide transportation to consumers often. Through the provision of intensive crisis intervention, engagement, and care coordination services, maintaining housing and mental health is the primary focus for this program. The Care Coordinator must hold a valid, State of Texas driver’s license and required insurance coverage. Staff are required to transport consumers using their personal vehicle and will be reimbursed for mileage by the Agency.

Your Role in Action

As a Care Coordinator for this unit, you will be:

Conducting comprehensive clinical assessments to determine service needs and track progress towards treatment goals.
Collaborating with the treatment team to develop personalized recovery plans, ensuring they are authorized and signed by a Licensed Practitioner of the Healing Arts (LPHA) for consumers on your caseload.
Ensuring that all provided services meet eligibility criteria and comply with agency and regulatory guidelines.
Delivering skills training and psychosocial rehabilitation services to address severe and persistent mental illness and related challenges that hinder individuals' functioning.
Providing crisis interventions to alleviate symptoms and prevent the need for more restrictive environments.
Assisting consumers in accessing necessary care and services based on their individual needs.
Conducting training and education sessions on mental illness, medication importance, and related information according to the Harris Center's curriculum.
Monitoring consumer progress towards treatment goals and compliance with eligibility requirements.
Meeting productivity standards set forth in operational guidelines.
Demonstrating ethical conduct in all clinical and professional activities.
Adhering to agency policies, procedures, and documentation requirements set by accrediting/regulatory bodies and performance contracts.

Education

What qualifications you will need:

Bachelor’s degree (B.A.) from four-year accredited college or university with a major in a social, behavioral, or human service field, including but not limited to: psychology, social work, medicine, nursing, rehabilitation, counseling, sociology, human development, gerontology, and educational psychology, required.

Experience

Minimum of one year experience in the mental health field, preferred.

Other Key Qualifications

Must maintain a valid Texas Driver's License and be insurable under Agency policy.
The ideal candidate will be required to transport consumers using their personal vehicle and will be reimbursed for mileage by the Agency.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Basic understanding of mental illness, common signs and symptoms and able to identify difficulties with coping in community settings.
Strong communication skills, listening and interpersonal skills above average, written documentation is clear, concise, well- constructed and grammatically correct.
Able to work collaboratively with others in a teamwork environment.
Effective time management and organizational skills. Able to execute standard word processing.
Must be able to work autonomously in a fast-paced environment.

What We Have To Offer

The Harris Center not only offers a competitive salary but also a suite of excellent benefits designed to enrich your life both professionally and personally. Imagine a future with a robust retirement plan complemented by our generous company matching – a testament to our investment in your long-term financial well-being. Experience the unique advantage of our prior service credit, accelerating your journey towards a more substantial Paid Time Off accrual, empowering you to enjoy well-deserved breaks.

Enjoy Cell Phone Discounts, exclusive entertainment deals through Tickets at Work, and a free Headspace subscription for mental wellness. Additionally, our Employee Assistance Program supports your overall well-being.

Take advantage of significant financial relief through student loan forgiveness as a valued member of The Harris Center team. As a qualifying entity, our employees are eligible for various student loan forgiveness programs, designed to alleviate the financial burdens associated with higher education.

What Else You Should Know

This posting is associated with position #2196-99106.
With travel to consumer homes, flexible scheduling, and an on-call status, every day will be filled with new challenges and experiences. You'll provide services in various environments, interact with individuals facing emotional or physical challenges, and overcome any obstacles with empathy and communication skills. Join us and embark on a rewarding journey of making a positive impact on others' lives, let the adventure begin!

About Us

The HARRIS CENTER is the state-designated Local Mental Health Authority and Local Intellectual and Developmental Disability (IDD) Authority serving Harris County, Texas. As the largest behavioral and developmental disability care center in Texas, The HARRIS CENTER provided care to over 90,000 people and has an annual budget of over $300 million.

As part of its mission to transform the lives of people with behavioral health and IDD needs in the third largest county in the United States, The HARRIS CENTER provides a full continuum of services at 80 different sites across Harris County. In addition, services are provided in more than 40 different languages as well as sign language in order to better serve what is one of the largest communities in the nation.

By utilizing the unique expertise of its more than 2,500 employees, The HARRIS CENTER is committed to meeting the behavioral health and IDD needs of Harris County residents and giving them hope to live to their fullest potential.

jobs.title: Foster Care Case Manager
jobs.description:
Our Company

StepStone Family & Youth Services

Overview

StepStone Family & Youth Services provides trauma informed, youth centered services to children and families involved in foster care. The Foster Care Case Manager plays a vital role in supporting youth and foster families through therapeutic case management, service coordination, and individualized support that promotes safety, stability, permanency, and positive outcomes.

We are seeking a compassionate and dedicated Foster Care Case Manager who is passionate about supporting children and families through trauma informed, strengths based, and family centered practices. This role is ideal for a professional who understands the impact of trauma, loss, and disrupted family systems and is committed to helping youth and families build resilience and long term success.

The Foster Care Case Manager works closely with foster families, biological families, treatment teams, schools, and community providers to support placement stability, emotional wellbeing, and coordinated care for youth in foster care placements. Through ongoing communication, advocacy, and service planning, this position helps ensure youth and families receive responsive and supportive services tailored to their unique needs.

The ideal candidate is organized, adaptable, empathetic, and committed to delivering high quality services while maintaining professionalism, compliance, and a trauma informed approach throughout all aspects of service delivery.

Responsibilities

The Foster Care Case Manager works under the supervision of the Program Manager. They are responsible for the delivery of case management services, individual and family counseling and training and supervision of foster families. The Foster Care Case Manager assists the Program Manager in developing individual treatment plans for troubled children and their families. They maintain weekly contact with the foster families, children, and bio-families and monitors the progress of the child and family throughout the placement. They assist with training, home studies, and evaluation of foster parents. The Foster Care Case Manager uses standardized tools to measure social and emotional progress and outcomes and prepares written treatment plans and progress reports.

PERSONAL WORK RELATIONSHIP: The Foster Care Case Manager makes decisions regarding the placement and treatment of neglected, abused, disturbed, and medically complex children. He or she will have good verbal and writing skills. They will be capable of working with children, parents, foster parents, client agencies and the courts. The Foster Care Case Manager will be creative, pragmatic, assertive, and know when to act independently and when to seek the advice of others.

EXAMPLES OF DUTIES. The position includes, but is not limited to, the following:

Reviews referrals and matches children with appropriate foster families.
Places children in state licensed or state certified foster homes.
Obtains all state and agency required documentation for child in care.
Provides weekly documented contact and at bi-weekly visits to child and foster home.
Visits each assigned child at least once each month away from the foster home.
Prepares a treatment plan for the child within 21 days of placement and quarterly thereafter.
Prepares monthly progress reports for assigned children.
Provides Independent Living training and monthly ILP progress reports for assigned clients.
Provides reunification services to the biological families when required by treatment plan.
Coordinates visitation of children with biological parents, siblings, and relatives.
Provides supervised visits with parents, siblings, and relative when required by court.
Acts as liaison person with placing agencies, schools, and other community agencies.
Attends court hearings and review hearings.
Attends staff meetings and treatment planning meetings as required.
Completes interviews, training and home studies on prospective foster parents as needed.
Attends conferences and seminars as required for annual training requirement.
Conducts/participates in two or more foster parent support group meetings each year.
Maintains flexible working hours and works weekends or holidays as needed.

Qualifications

The Foster Care Case Manager has a bachelor’s degree in social work, sociology, psychology, counseling, or related human services field and two years’ experience working with children and families. A bachelor’s degree in social work, sociology, psychology, counseling, or related human services field and five years’ experience with a placing agency working with troubled children and families may be consider in lieu of a graduate degree.

About Our Line Of Business

StepStone Family and Youth Services, an affiliate of BrightSpring Health Services, provides the full spectrum of support to children in need of alternative, safer, and more positive living environments with residential and family services. StepStone connects children and youth who need homes with foster families, as well as foster care training, respite care and support services. For young adults transitioning from foster care to independent living, StepStone provides personalized guidance and training on basic life skills, including money management and education. For more information, please visit www.stepstoneyouth.com . Follow us on Facebook and LinkedIn .

jobs.description:
Primary Purpose:
The primary role of the Medical Care Coordinator I (MCC) is to schedule and coordinate medical, dental, and emergency care for crew members who live and work aboard commercial shipping vessels. This role supports a global, 24/7 operation and requires the ability to work effectively across different time zones and under pressure.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities

To perform this job successfully, the Medical Care Coordinator I must be able to perform each essential duty and responsibility listed below satisfactorily:
Triage new medical requests, correctly collecting required client, patient, port, and ship information. Accurately enter information into case management system.
Schedule medical, dental, emergency care, and prescription medication services using SphereMD providers; find alternate providers when necessary while continually updating proprietary database in real time.
Effectively coordinate transportation to appointments with transportation vendors, vessel agents, and other involved parties around the vessel’s schedule.
Effectively and accurately relay information between medical providers, agents, vessel interests, and insurance companies via email or by phone, documenting all actions in case management system.
Keep track of all related costs by updating case management system in real time.
Monitor email updates concerning cases throughout the day, responding as required to facilitate completion of each client case.
Ensure accuracy of email communication by double checking job, patient, and vessel on each communication.
Work maritime on-call coverage per protocol, responding to after-hours and emergency care needs as part of a rotating on-call schedule.
Juggle multiple priorities throughout the day, including frequent task-switching and managing interruptions without losing focus.
Other duties as assigned.

Requirements:
Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required of Medical Care Coordinator I for this position:
Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational skills with attention to detail.
Ability to work well under pressure in a complex and rapidly evolving environment.
Ability to maintain consistent customer service focus on producing an outcome
Ability to multi-task and prioritize (and re-prioritize, as needed).
Ability to remain focused while starting and stopping tasks frequently throughout the day.
Ability to take a case, conceive a plan to solve all elements of the case, and implement changes as necessary.
Proven ability to manage competing priorities and shift focus seamlessly.
Ability to work both independently and interdependently with staff and team members with limited supervision.
Ability to maintain a friendly, professional demeanor while working with various personalities and cultures.
Consistent, dependable work effort and a positive work attitude.
Ability to maintain regular and reliable attendance and punctuality.
An attitude of respect for others and a commitment to get the job done.
Excellent computer skills in Microsoft Office and ability to learn new software. QuickBooks experience is a plus.

Additional Expectations:

Participation in after-hours, weekend, and holiday on-call rotations is required to support the organization’s 24/7 global operations.

Minimum Experience Required

To perform this job successfully, the following experience is required for the Medical Care Coordinator I:
Experience: At least 3 years of experience performing heavy administrative work is required. Prior experience in a healthcare or medical setting is preferred but is not required. Prior Customer service experience is required.
Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience is required.

Performance Evaluations:
Evaluations will be conducted no less than annually to evaluate how well the employee performed their essential duties and to measure overall performance in the primary areas of:
Job description duties and responsibilities.
Adhering to specific job KPI’s (key performance indicators).
Overall job knowledge and performance.
Exemplifying behaviors and actions that embody our company Core Values and Operating Principles:

Core Values:

CARE – Choosing a supportive and compassionate approach to our work and to our relationships that enables optimal outcomes.
INNOVATION – Having an open mindset that welcomes and embraces new ideas and creative problem solving that enhances processes, services, and experiences.
COLLABORATION – Working together to create purposeful connections, internally and externally, to solve problems and achieve goals through sharing varied skillsets, perspectives, and ideas.
TRUST – Acting with integrity by demonstrating dependability, respect, and honesty in all that we do and fostering a safe environment for authentic connections that enable mutual trust.
COMMUNICATION – Prioritizing a pro-active, accurate, and timely approach to communication to ensure the success of our engagements in every interaction.

Operating Principles:

ETHICAL INTEGRITY – Integrity cannot be compromised. We do the right thing by our patients, customers, and team. We never take short-cuts. We approach our work and relationships with ethical integrity – it guides our actions and choices.
ACCOUNTABILITY – Everyone must be accountable for producing to their potential every day. We take responsibility for our actions and choices. We follow through on what we say we will do. We are present.
EXCELLENCE – We strive to do our very best in every action and choice we make every day. We believe in always learning, growing, and sharing with each other. We celebrate our successes and acknowledge when and how we can do better next time.
GOOD INTENTION – We start from the belief that everyone acts with the best intentions. We do not assume anything but instead as questions to gain clarity and understanding. It is from this vantage point that we engage with each other and with our customers.
ADAPTABILITY – We know that change is constant. We adapt when needed and pivot to meet the ever-changing needs of our customers and the business.

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the position, but rather an illustrative list of expectations. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change, or new ones may be assigned at any time with or without notice.
PHYSICAL DEMAND:
This position requires physical effort and work positions for the Medical Care Coordinator I as listed below to be able to perform the essential functions of the job acceptably:
The physical effort typically applied in this job includes:
Lifting up to 15 pounds
Carrying up to 15 pounds

Program Coordinator - Youth Gymnastics

POSITION SUMMARY:
This position supports the work of the Y, a leading nonprofit committed to strengthening community through youth development, healthy living, and social responsibility. The Youth Gymnastics Program Coordinator is responsible for overseeing daily program operations, supporting and developing staff, and ensuring a safe, positive, and engaging environment for participants. This position promotes quality instruction, encourages staff growth, and helps create an atmosphere that builds confidence, skill development, and self-esteem in children.

EDUCATION AND YEARS OF EXPERIENCE REQUIRED:
Minimum 18 years of age. High School Diploma or equivalent required. Previous gymnastics, ninja, or coaching experience in a gymnastics/ninja facility is a plus;  2-3 years of related experience preferred, with demonstrated ability to organize, support and supervise staff.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

Provides leadership, supervision, and support to gymnastics and ninja staff while ensuring a safe, positive, and engaging environment for all participants. 
Models and promotes the YMCA’s mission of developing a healthy mind, body, and spirit through quality recreation programming. 
Trains, mentors, and provides feedback to instructors and coaches to ensure consistent instruction, safety practices, and participant engagement. 
Oversees daily class operations, including staff coverage, class quality, equipment use, and program expectations. 
Assists with the development, implementation, and evaluation of gymnastics and ninja curriculum, lesson plans, and program improvements. 
Uses good judgment, flexibility, creativity, and sensitivity when addressing staff, participant, and parent needs. 
Ensures staff follow YMCA policies, procedures, Code of Conduct standards, and appropriate behavior management practices. 
Communicates effectively with participants, parents, staff, and leadership to address questions, concerns, and program needs. 
Monitors class attendance, staff schedules, and program records to maintain accurate documentation. 
Maintains a clean, organized, and safe gymnastics/ninja environment while ensuring equipment and facility standards are met. 
Assists with staff scheduling, finding coverage, and communicating staffing needs with the Gymnastics Director. 
Supports hiring, onboarding, training, and ongoing development of gymnastics and ninja team members. 
Teaches gymnastics and ninja classes as needed, providing quality instruction, skill development, and a positive experience for participants. 
Ensures compliance with safety regulations, emergency procedures, and risk management practices; reports concerns to the Gymnastics Director and Risk Management as needed. 
Supports special events, competitions, camps, clinics, evaluations, and scholarship fundraising activities. 
Attends required trainings, meetings, and professional development opportunities as directed by Countryside YMCA and the Gymnastics Director. 
Performs other duties as assigned or required by business necessity.

Qualifications

REQUIRED SKILLS/ABILITIES :
Ability to demonstrate and teach a variety of gymnastics and ninja skills while ensuring proper progressions and safety practices. 
Reliable and punctual attendance with the ability to support daily program operations. 
Creative problem-solving skills with strong verbal and written communication abilities. 
Ability to supervise participants and staff with confidence, enthusiasm, and a focus on safety and positive experiences. 
Ability to provide leadership, guidance, and support to instructors while maintaining program quality. 
Must be at least 18 years of age and successfully complete a criminal background check.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: 

Ability to plan, lead, supervise, and participate in a variety of gymnastics and ninja activities in an indoor recreation setting. Noise levels will vary depending on participant activity and program operations within the gymnastics center. Role may require carrying, kneeling, pushing, pulling, sitting, climbing, lifting, running, stooping, crouching, standing, and walking. Must have the physical ability to assist participants, demonstrate skills when needed, and respond quickly to safety concerns or emergency situations.

REASONABLE ACCOMMODATIONS STATEMENT 

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.  Reasonable Accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
ABUSE PREVENTION STATEMENT: 

Countryside YMCA is committed to providing a safe environment for all children and vulnerable individuals in our care. We follow best practices for abuse prevention, including thorough screening, ongoing training, and clear behavioral expectations for staff and volunteers. We have a zero-tolerance policy for abuse and take all allegations and concerns very seriously. All employees are required to follow our child protection policies, complete required training, and report any suspicious or inappropriate behavior immediately.

Assist planning, execution, and management of program cost, schedule, and performance for Nuclear Systems Integration Division’s branches (Tail Kit Assembly [TKA], Weapon Systems Integration and Test, Logistics, or Program Management) depending on background and experience.

If you like solving complex international trade problems using your deep compliance skills, this is the opportunity for you! The Senior International Trade Compliance Analyst provides expert leadership in ensuring the company's adherence to U.S. and international trade regulations. This role involves strategic oversight of compliance initiatives, managing highly complex export/import authorizations, and acting as a senior advisor on compliance matters.

As SNC's corporate team, we provide the company and its business areas with strategic direction and business support spanning executive management, finance and accounting, operations, human resources, legal, IT, information security, facilities, marketing, and communications.

Responsibilities

Design, develop, and maintain compliance dashboards, reports, and metrics to identify trends, anomalies, risks, and drive actionable insights and improvements to leadership and stakeholders.
Develop and present key trade compliance program metrics and performance indicators to senior leadership on a recurring basis.
Build and maintain automated reporting tools to reduce manual effort and improve data accuracy and timeliness.
Translate complex regulatory and operational data into clear, concise visual reports for both technical and non-technical audiences.
Lead and support the integration of trade compliance tools and systems with internal ERP, logistics, and business platforms.
Collaborate with IT and business operations teams to design, test, and implement system enhancements that support compliance workflows.
Serve as a subject matter expert and provide ongoing technical support for international trade compliance tools and systems
Identify opportunities to leverage technology to streamline and automate compliance processes.
Document system integration workflows, data flows, and technical specifications to ensure international trade requirement integration, operational continuity, and auditability.
Plan, manage, and execute trade compliance projects from initiation through completion, ensuring deliverables are met on time and within scope.
Coordinate cross-functional teams including legal, logistics, engineering, security, and IT to drive compliance initiatives forward.
Develop project plans, timelines, risk registers, organizational change management (OCM) strategy, and status reports for compliance initiatives.
Serve as a liaison between compliance, business, and technology stakeholders to align priorities and communicate project progress.
Support and manage continuous improvement efforts within the trade compliance function.

Qualifications You Must Have

Bachelor’s degree in a related field (Business, Supply Chain, Data Analytics, Information Systems, International Trade, or similar).
5+ years of experience in international trade compliance, data analytics, or a related field.
Relevant experience can be considered as a substitute for the required educational qualifications. In the absence of a degree, a minimum of 9 years of related experience is required.
Higher level relevant degree may substitute for experience.
Demonstrated experience in data analytics, report building, or business intelligence tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau, Excel, SQL, or similar).
Experience with maximizing MS365 capabilities (Sharepoint, Powerapps, Powerautomate, Copilot, etc.)
Experience supporting or leading system integration projects or technology implementations.
Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
Experience working in multi-disciplinary, cross-functional teams.

Qualifications We Prefer

Experience in the Aerospace and Defense industry.
Certification in Trade Compliance, Project Management, or Data Analytics.
Advanced knowledge of trade compliance platforms such as OCR EASE, DECCS, SNAP-R, and ACE.
Experience with ERP systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle, Costpoint) and their integration with trade compliance workflows.
Working knowledge of ITAR, EAR, Foreign Trade Regulations (FTR), Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA), and other relevant trade regulations.
Proficiency in scripting or programming languages for data automation (e.g., Python, R, or similar).
Experience developing AI use cases and building agentic workflows.
Familiarity with Agile, Waterfall, or other structured project management methodologies.

Essential Functions

Ability to work on a computer for extended periods.
Requires good hand and finger dexterity for data entry.
Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing.
Must be able to travel up to 10% of the time.
Ability to work in an office or hybrid environment.

jobs.description:

No

The supervisor will work with each student employee to establish a schedule that accommodates their class schedule.

Position Introduction

The Dodge Family College of Arts and Sciences Dean's Office is seeking two undergraduate students to join its Data Analysis team as Student Data Analysts.

This position provides students with practical experience in data analysis, research, reporting, and data visualization. Student Data Analysts will work with institutional data and support projects that inform decision-making across the College. Students will receive hands-on training and regular guidance as they develop skills in Excel, Power BI, data validation, analytical reasoning, and professional communication.

We are especially interested in students who would like to remain in the position for multiple semesters, allowing them to continue developing their skills and take on increasingly independent work.

Responsibilities

Build and maintain reports, dashboards, charts, and analytical models using Excel and Power BI.
Retrieve, organize, review, and validate institutional data.
Assist with enrollment, student, academic program, and other College-level analyses.
Respond to data and reporting requests from departments and Dean's Office leadership.
Research and investigate unexpected trends or inconsistencies in data.
Learn to query databases and work with institutional data sources.
Document data sources, calculations, assumptions, and analytical methods.
Summarize findings in clear language for non-technical audiences.
Assist with longer-term analytical projects from initial research through final presentation.
Manage multiple assignments and deadlines.
Handle confidential student and personnel information in accordance with FERPA and University policies.
Perform other related duties as assigned.

Student analysts will learn to answer three important questions about their work:

How did you arrive at that number?
Where did the data come from?
How do we know it's right?

What You'll Learn

Develop advanced Excel and Power BI skills.
Learn how professional analysts approach and validate data.
Work with real-world datasets and business questions.
Improve analytical writing and data visualization skills.
Present findings to College leadership and departmental administrators.
Complete projects that can be discussed in future job or graduate school interviews.
Receive regular feedback and professional development from the Executive Director.

Students who demonstrate strong performance and increased proficiency may be considered for additional responsibilities and advancement opportunities, subject to University processes and available funding.

Students from all DFCAS majors are encouraged to apply. Advanced data-analysis experience is not required. We are looking for students who are curious, careful, willing to learn, and interested in understanding not only what the numbers show, but why. Students with at least two semesters remaining at OU are especially encouraged to apply.

Selection Process

We want to see how you like to solve problems. The interview includes a short data-analysis exercise: you'll build a simple chart and write a brief interpretation of the data, and then we'll talk through it together. We're evaluating analytical thinking, attention to detail, and communication — not advanced Excel skills, and not how you perform under pressure. If you need help with Excel, just ask.

Use Of AI

AI tools may be used as part of the application process, interview exercise, and position when appropriate.

Applicants should be prepared to explain how they used AI and how they reviewed or verified its output. AI is considered a tool to support analytical work, not a replacement for independent judgment.

All use of AI while working with University information must comply with applicable University requirements regarding confidentiality, FERPA, information security, and institutional data.

Required Education And Experience

Must be currently enrolled in the Fall Term as a student at the University of Oklahoma.

Hiring contingent upon verification of current student status.

Must be a student in the Dodge Family College of Arts and Sciences.

Skills

Basic familiarity with Microsoft Excel.
Strong written communication skills.
Attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
Ability to think critically and solve problems.
Ability to learn new software and analytical methods.
Ability to maintain confidentiality.
Ability to maintain a consistent weekly work schedule.

Department Preferences

Coursework or experience in one or more of the following areas is helpful but not required:

Statistics
Economics
Research methods
Data analysis
Quantitative reasoning
Computer science or programming
Business analytics
Social science research
Research and analytical writing

Role Description

The Community Engagement Coordinator is a full-time, on-site position based in Billings, Montana. This highly people-focused role serves as a primary connection between Habitat for Humanity Mid-Yellowstone Valley and the volunteers, organizations, businesses, and community members who help advance our mission.

A significant focus of this position is volunteer recruitment, coordination, engagement, and stewardship. The Coordinator works to ensure volunteers have a positive experience from their first inquiry through their day of service and beyond. This includes recruiting individual and group volunteers, coordinating schedules and opportunities, communicating expectations, welcoming volunteers, supporting them while they serve, and helping build long-term relationships that encourage continued involvement with Habitat.

This is not strictly a desk-based outreach position. The Community Engagement Coordinator must be comfortable working alongside volunteers in a variety of environments, including active residential construction sites. The Coordinator may assist with volunteer check-in, orientation, site preparation, hospitality, safety communication, and general volunteer support throughout the build day.

Additional responsibilities include developing relationships with community organizations, businesses, faith communities, schools, civic groups, and other partners; coordinating community events and informational sessions; representing Habitat at public events and meetings; and supporting communication efforts through newsletters, social media, outreach campaigns, and other materials.

The Coordinator will also maintain volunteer and community engagement records, track participation and engagement metrics, gather feedback, and collaborate closely with Habitat's construction, development, ReStore, and leadership teams to connect community members with meaningful opportunities to participate in Habitat's mission.

Key Responsibilities

- Recruit and engage individual volunteers, corporate teams, faith communities, civic organizations, schools, and other community groups.
- Coordinate volunteer inquiries, registration, scheduling, confirmations, reminders, and follow-up communication.
- Welcome, orient, and support volunteers to create a safe, organized, inclusive, and meaningful service experience.
- Maintain regular communication with volunteers and develop strategies to encourage volunteer retention and continued engagement.
- Work directly with construction staff to coordinate volunteer needs and schedules for Habitat build sites.
- Be present on active construction sites to assist with volunteer check-in, orientation, hospitality, communication, and day-of support.
- Develop a basic understanding of Habitat construction activities in order to effectively communicate with and serve volunteers.
- Build and maintain relationships with community organizations, businesses, faith communities, schools, residents, and other partners.
- Plan and coordinate community outreach activities, volunteer events, informational sessions, and special events.
- Represent Habitat for Humanity Mid-Yellowstone Valley at community meetings, presentations, volunteer fairs, and public events.
- Develop and coordinate outreach communications, including newsletters, social media content, volunteer communications, and promotional materials.
- Maintain accurate volunteer and community engagement records and contact databases.
- Track volunteer participation, outreach activities, and other engagement metrics to help evaluate and strengthen community engagement efforts.
- Gather feedback from volunteers and community partners and identify opportunities to improve the volunteer experience.
- Collaborate across Habitat departments to connect volunteers and community partners with opportunities that best match organizational needs.
- Perform other mission-related duties as needed in support of Habitat's programs, events, and community initiatives.

Qualifications

- Demonstrated experience in volunteer management, volunteer recruitment, community engagement, community outreach, customer service, or relationship-based work.
- Strong interpersonal skills and a genuine ability to make volunteers and community members feel welcomed, valued, informed, and appreciated.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including public speaking, group facilitation, and active listening.
- Experience coordinating volunteers, events, schedules, logistics, or community activities.
- Ability to build and maintain relationships with people from diverse backgrounds, organizations, and sectors of the community.
- Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple projects, schedules, and priorities.
- Ability to work collaboratively as part of a team while also independently managing assigned responsibilities.
- Comfort using basic office software, databases, email communication, and social media platforms.
- Previous nonprofit, volunteer management, community development, construction, social services, hospitality, or related experience is preferred.
- High school diploma or equivalent required; post-secondary education in nonprofit management, communications, social work, community development, volunteer administration, or a related field is an asset.

Physical and Work Environment Requirements

This position includes work in an office environment, throughout the community, at special events, and on active residential construction sites.

Candidates must be willing and able to:

- Work outdoors in varying weather conditions.
- Navigate active construction sites, including uneven terrain and unfinished structures.
- Stand and walk for extended periods during volunteer builds and events.
- Occasionally lift, carry, or move supplies and materials associated with volunteer activities and events.
- Wear required personal protective equipment and follow all Habitat construction-site safety procedures.
- Work occasional evenings or weekends to support volunteer builds, community events, and organizational activities.
- Travel locally throughout the Mid-Yellowstone Valley, with reliable transportation for outreach and volunteer activities.

Construction experience is not required. A willingness to learn, participate, serve others, and be comfortable in a hands-on environment is.

What Success Looks Like

The successful Community Engagement Coordinator understands that volunteer management is more than filling available shifts. It is about building relationships.

Volunteers should leave a Habitat experience knowing their time mattered, understanding the impact they helped create, and wanting to come back. This position helps create that experience while building a stronger network of people and organizations invested in Habitat's mission and the communities we serve.

Description

Positive Impact Health Centers (PIHC)
is a community leader in providing HIV prevention, care and treatment services. The PIHC model of care assures that persons with HIV have access to medical, pharmacy, dental, behavioral health and social services, providing the best opportunity for patients to achieve high-quality health outcomes.

JOB SUMMARY:
The Medical Case Manager (MCM) will provide medical case management services to eligible adult clinic patients at Positive Impact Health Centers, following applicable funding guidelines and best practice care models. The MCM will function as an integral member of an interdisciplinary team which may include the following: medical provider, behavioral health clinician, medication access specialist, clinical pharmacist, and supportive services staff (Community Health Worker, Patient Navigator, Retention/Adherence Manager).

This position description should not be interpreted as all-inclusive. It is intended to identify the major responsibilities and requirements of this position. The incumbent may be requested to perform job-related responsibilities and tasks other than those stated in this position description.

Essential Functions

Duties and Responsibilities:

Learn and remain current on practice issues related to HIV/AIDS, related medical diagnoses, and medical case management.
Provide medical case management services to identified patients of the clinic program, following medical case management guidelines established by HRSA/Ryan White and the Metropolitan Atlanta HIV Health Services Planning Council.
Complete biopsychosocial assessments with new and returning patients, utilizing required screening tools established by the Metropolitan Atlanta HIV Health Services Planning Council and Ryan White/HRSA.
Provide medical case management services to an average caseload size of 70 patients: develop a comprehensive Individualized Service Plan (ISP); provide ongoing monitoring of ISP with each patient to assess the efficacy of the plan; coordinate services to meet goals of the service plan.
Perform periodic re-evaluations and revisions/adaptations of service plans.
Provide adherence and retention counseling to ensure patients maintain health care.
Identify gaps in core and supportive services, including care resources, mental health, substance abuse, housing, nutrition, and transportation
Coordinate referrals and follow-up for medical and non-medical services.
Actively participate as part of an interdisciplinary care team to assess patient care needs and coordinate service referrals.
Assist patients with applications and ongoing eligibility for medication access programs (i.e. ADAP and pharmaceutical assistance programs), as needed to support clinic staff.
Assist Self-Managed patients with social service questions and related needs.
Develop network of additional community resources.
Document patient information, activities, referrals and consultations in a timely and accurate manner, through the use of the agency’s electronic medical record system and related reporting software.
Abide by all state, federal laws and agency policies as related to confidentiality and Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).
Assist the agency administration in the development of long-range plans, including goals and objectives, as directed by supervisor.
Abides by all agency policies and procedures, including conflict of interest policy.
Additional duties as assigned.

Requirements

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

Strong social work, nursing, or case management skills, including the ability to obtain a comprehensive psychosocial assessment and assist adult clients with the development of an individualized service plan;
Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to communicate effectively in a multi-cultural setting including target populations, volunteers, agency staff, and agency Board members;
Proficient computer skills for word processing, data entry, documentation, and navigation of Internet;
Comprehensive and up-to-date knowledge of HIV medical and case management fundamentals preferred;
Ability to adapt work style to accommodate both solitary and collaborative tasks;
Ability to function independently without close supervision;
Excellent time management techniques;
Consistent follow-through to completion of assigned tasks

Minimum Qualifications

Social service or nursing degree from an accredited university program. BSW or MSW in social work preferred.

Experience

Minimum of one year’s experience in a service delivery setting, with an emphasis on locating, coordinating and developing supportive services for identified clients across a broad psychosocial continuum is required.
Professional experience working in a medical setting is preferred.
Minimum of one year’s previous professional experience working with adults living with HIV is preferred.
Previous professional experience with Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system documentation preferred.
Written and verbal fluency in Spanish is highly preferred.

License/Licensure

Licensure, or licensure-eligible, as applicable to degree (e.g. LMSW or LCSW if hold an MSW degree)

Physical Demands:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to walk, use hands to finger, handle, or operate computers, objects, tools, or controls and reach with hands and arms.

The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 30 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus.

Recreational drugs, weapons and violence are not permitted on agency property or at any agency events or programs.

Join Our Team as a Foster Care Coordinator!

Childhelp Tennessee’s Foster Family Services program is seeking a full-time Care Coordinator for our Knoxville office location. Please consider joining our team as we make a positive difference in the lives of foster children and their families in East TN!

Childhelp provides therapeutic foster home services to children in state custody as well as services to their families in the hope that we can achieve permanency for these children by safely reuniting them with their birth families, or providing these children with a permanent adoptive family if reunification is not possible.

Besides serving as a “case manager”, our Care Coordinators serve as active therapeutic mentors and teachers for ALL of our clients, provide crisis intervention when/as needed and advocate for the best interest of the children and families we serve.

Making regular, timely home visits to our foster homes to check on the children and foster families to ensure that everyone is doing well and getting their needs met in an excellent way
Engaging, teaching and encouraging birth parents to complete the Permanency Plan goal in an effort to safely reunite children and families whenever possible

Assisting our foster parents in obtaining and scheduling needed services for the child(ren) in their care
Providing and/or displaying excellent customer service, organizational and communication (verbal and written) skills
The ability to be creative, innovative, flexible and solution-focused in a fast-paced environment
The ability to be a supportive, encouraging member of the staff team and treatment team

Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Psychology, Counseling or a closely-related field is required
Minimum of 21 years of age
