Brief Description

Are you ready to make a real difference in people's lives? Join the Harris Center for Mental Health and IDD as a Care Coordinator
. Under the general direction of the Clinical Team Lead, Care Coordinator (CC) provides case management and coordination of care services. The Care Coordinator will provide all services within the community for individuals participating in a housing program affiliated with the Coalition for the Homeless. The CC will provide care coordination and case management services as part of a multidisciplinary team that includes a Master Level Clinician or LPHA and LCDC. Peer support services are also offered within the program. The CC will be expected to provide transportation to consumers often. Through the provision of intensive crisis intervention, engagement, and care coordination services, maintaining housing and mental health is the primary focus for this program. The Care Coordinator must hold a valid, State of Texas driver’s license and required insurance coverage. Staff are required to transport consumers using their personal vehicle and will be reimbursed for mileage by the Agency.

Your Role in Action

As a Care Coordinator for this unit, you will be:

Conducting comprehensive clinical assessments to determine service needs and track progress towards treatment goals.
Collaborating with the treatment team to develop personalized recovery plans, ensuring they are authorized and signed by a Licensed Practitioner of the Healing Arts (LPHA) for consumers on your caseload.
Ensuring that all provided services meet eligibility criteria and comply with agency and regulatory guidelines.
Delivering skills training and psychosocial rehabilitation services to address severe and persistent mental illness and related challenges that hinder individuals' functioning.
Providing crisis interventions to alleviate symptoms and prevent the need for more restrictive environments.
Assisting consumers in accessing necessary care and services based on their individual needs.
Conducting training and education sessions on mental illness, medication importance, and related information according to the Harris Center's curriculum.
Monitoring consumer progress towards treatment goals and compliance with eligibility requirements.
Meeting productivity standards set forth in operational guidelines.
Demonstrating ethical conduct in all clinical and professional activities.
Adhering to agency policies, procedures, and documentation requirements set by accrediting/regulatory bodies and performance contracts.

Education

What qualifications you will need:

Bachelor’s degree (B.A.) from four-year accredited college or university with a major in a social, behavioral, or human service field, including but not limited to: psychology, social work, medicine, nursing, rehabilitation, counseling, sociology, human development, gerontology, and educational psychology, required.

Experience

Minimum of one year experience in the mental health field, preferred.

Other Key Qualifications

Must maintain a valid Texas Driver's License and be insurable under Agency policy.
The ideal candidate will be required to transport consumers using their personal vehicle and will be reimbursed for mileage by the Agency.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Basic understanding of mental illness, common signs and symptoms and able to identify difficulties with coping in community settings.
Strong communication skills, listening and interpersonal skills above average, written documentation is clear, concise, well- constructed and grammatically correct.
Able to work collaboratively with others in a teamwork environment.
Effective time management and organizational skills. Able to execute standard word processing.
Must be able to work autonomously in a fast-paced environment.

What We Have To Offer

The Harris Center not only offers a competitive salary but also a suite of excellent benefits designed to enrich your life both professionally and personally. Imagine a future with a robust retirement plan complemented by our generous company matching – a testament to our investment in your long-term financial well-being. Experience the unique advantage of our prior service credit, accelerating your journey towards a more substantial Paid Time Off accrual, empowering you to enjoy well-deserved breaks.

Enjoy Cell Phone Discounts, exclusive entertainment deals through Tickets at Work, and a free Headspace subscription for mental wellness. Additionally, our Employee Assistance Program supports your overall well-being.

Take advantage of significant financial relief through student loan forgiveness as a valued member of The Harris Center team. As a qualifying entity, our employees are eligible for various student loan forgiveness programs, designed to alleviate the financial burdens associated with higher education.

What Else You Should Know

This posting is associated with position #2196-99106.
With travel to consumer homes, flexible scheduling, and an on-call status, every day will be filled with new challenges and experiences. You'll provide services in various environments, interact with individuals facing emotional or physical challenges, and overcome any obstacles with empathy and communication skills. Join us and embark on a rewarding journey of making a positive impact on others' lives, let the adventure begin!

About Us

The HARRIS CENTER is the state-designated Local Mental Health Authority and Local Intellectual and Developmental Disability (IDD) Authority serving Harris County, Texas. As the largest behavioral and developmental disability care center in Texas, The HARRIS CENTER provided care to over 90,000 people and has an annual budget of over $300 million.

As part of its mission to transform the lives of people with behavioral health and IDD needs in the third largest county in the United States, The HARRIS CENTER provides a full continuum of services at 80 different sites across Harris County. In addition, services are provided in more than 40 different languages as well as sign language in order to better serve what is one of the largest communities in the nation.

By utilizing the unique expertise of its more than 2,500 employees, The HARRIS CENTER is committed to meeting the behavioral health and IDD needs of Harris County residents and giving them hope to live to their fullest potential.

new_jobs.title: Foster Care Case Manager
new_jobs.description:
Our Company

StepStone Family & Youth Services

Overview

StepStone Family & Youth Services provides trauma informed, youth centered services to children and families involved in foster care. The Foster Care Case Manager plays a vital role in supporting youth and foster families through therapeutic case management, service coordination, and individualized support that promotes safety, stability, permanency, and positive outcomes.

We are seeking a compassionate and dedicated Foster Care Case Manager who is passionate about supporting children and families through trauma informed, strengths based, and family centered practices. This role is ideal for a professional who understands the impact of trauma, loss, and disrupted family systems and is committed to helping youth and families build resilience and long term success.

The Foster Care Case Manager works closely with foster families, biological families, treatment teams, schools, and community providers to support placement stability, emotional wellbeing, and coordinated care for youth in foster care placements. Through ongoing communication, advocacy, and service planning, this position helps ensure youth and families receive responsive and supportive services tailored to their unique needs.

The ideal candidate is organized, adaptable, empathetic, and committed to delivering high quality services while maintaining professionalism, compliance, and a trauma informed approach throughout all aspects of service delivery.

Responsibilities

The Foster Care Case Manager works under the supervision of the Program Manager. They are responsible for the delivery of case management services, individual and family counseling and training and supervision of foster families. The Foster Care Case Manager assists the Program Manager in developing individual treatment plans for troubled children and their families. They maintain weekly contact with the foster families, children, and bio-families and monitors the progress of the child and family throughout the placement. They assist with training, home studies, and evaluation of foster parents. The Foster Care Case Manager uses standardized tools to measure social and emotional progress and outcomes and prepares written treatment plans and progress reports.

PERSONAL WORK RELATIONSHIP: The Foster Care Case Manager makes decisions regarding the placement and treatment of neglected, abused, disturbed, and medically complex children. He or she will have good verbal and writing skills. They will be capable of working with children, parents, foster parents, client agencies and the courts. The Foster Care Case Manager will be creative, pragmatic, assertive, and know when to act independently and when to seek the advice of others.

EXAMPLES OF DUTIES. The position includes, but is not limited to, the following:

Reviews referrals and matches children with appropriate foster families.
Places children in state licensed or state certified foster homes.
Obtains all state and agency required documentation for child in care.
Provides weekly documented contact and at bi-weekly visits to child and foster home.
Visits each assigned child at least once each month away from the foster home.
Prepares a treatment plan for the child within 21 days of placement and quarterly thereafter.
Prepares monthly progress reports for assigned children.
Provides Independent Living training and monthly ILP progress reports for assigned clients.
Provides reunification services to the biological families when required by treatment plan.
Coordinates visitation of children with biological parents, siblings, and relatives.
Provides supervised visits with parents, siblings, and relative when required by court.
Acts as liaison person with placing agencies, schools, and other community agencies.
Attends court hearings and review hearings.
Attends staff meetings and treatment planning meetings as required.
Completes interviews, training and home studies on prospective foster parents as needed.
Attends conferences and seminars as required for annual training requirement.
Conducts/participates in two or more foster parent support group meetings each year.
Maintains flexible working hours and works weekends or holidays as needed.

Qualifications

The Foster Care Case Manager has a bachelor’s degree in social work, sociology, psychology, counseling, or related human services field and two years’ experience working with children and families. A bachelor’s degree in social work, sociology, psychology, counseling, or related human services field and five years’ experience with a placing agency working with troubled children and families may be consider in lieu of a graduate degree.

About Our Line Of Business

StepStone Family and Youth Services, an affiliate of BrightSpring Health Services, provides the full spectrum of support to children in need of alternative, safer, and more positive living environments with residential and family services. StepStone connects children and youth who need homes with foster families, as well as foster care training, respite care and support services. For young adults transitioning from foster care to independent living, StepStone provides personalized guidance and training on basic life skills, including money management and education. For more information, please visit www.stepstoneyouth.com . Follow us on Facebook and LinkedIn .

Primary Purpose:
The primary role of the Medical Care Coordinator I (MCC) is to schedule and coordinate medical, dental, and emergency care for crew members who live and work aboard commercial shipping vessels. This role supports a global, 24/7 operation and requires the ability to work effectively across different time zones and under pressure.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities

To perform this job successfully, the Medical Care Coordinator I must be able to perform each essential duty and responsibility listed below satisfactorily:
Triage new medical requests, correctly collecting required client, patient, port, and ship information. Accurately enter information into case management system.
Schedule medical, dental, emergency care, and prescription medication services using SphereMD providers; find alternate providers when necessary while continually updating proprietary database in real time.
Effectively coordinate transportation to appointments with transportation vendors, vessel agents, and other involved parties around the vessel’s schedule.
Effectively and accurately relay information between medical providers, agents, vessel interests, and insurance companies via email or by phone, documenting all actions in case management system.
Keep track of all related costs by updating case management system in real time.
Monitor email updates concerning cases throughout the day, responding as required to facilitate completion of each client case.
Ensure accuracy of email communication by double checking job, patient, and vessel on each communication.
Work maritime on-call coverage per protocol, responding to after-hours and emergency care needs as part of a rotating on-call schedule.
Juggle multiple priorities throughout the day, including frequent task-switching and managing interruptions without losing focus.
Other duties as assigned.

Requirements:
Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required of Medical Care Coordinator I for this position:
Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational skills with attention to detail.
Ability to work well under pressure in a complex and rapidly evolving environment.
Ability to maintain consistent customer service focus on producing an outcome
Ability to multi-task and prioritize (and re-prioritize, as needed).
Ability to remain focused while starting and stopping tasks frequently throughout the day.
Ability to take a case, conceive a plan to solve all elements of the case, and implement changes as necessary.
Proven ability to manage competing priorities and shift focus seamlessly.
Ability to work both independently and interdependently with staff and team members with limited supervision.
Ability to maintain a friendly, professional demeanor while working with various personalities and cultures.
Consistent, dependable work effort and a positive work attitude.
Ability to maintain regular and reliable attendance and punctuality.
An attitude of respect for others and a commitment to get the job done.

Experience: At least 3 years of experience performing heavy administrative work is required. Prior experience in a healthcare or medical setting is preferred but is not required. Prior Customer service experience is required.

new_jobs.description:
Program Coordinator - Youth Gymnastics

POSITION SUMMARY:
This position supports the work of the Y, a leading nonprofit committed to strengthening community through youth development, healthy living, and social responsibility. The Youth Gymnastics Program Coordinator is responsible for overseeing daily program operations, supporting and developing staff, and ensuring a safe, positive, and engaging environment for participants. This position promotes quality instruction, encourages staff growth, and helps create an atmosphere that builds confidence, skill development, and self-esteem in children.

EDUCATION AND YEARS OF EXPERIENCE REQUIRED:
Minimum 18 years of age. High School Diploma or equivalent required. Previous gymnastics, ninja, or coaching experience in a gymnastics/ninja facility is a plus;  2-3 years of related experience preferred, with demonstrated ability to organize, support and supervise staff.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

Provides leadership, supervision, and support to gymnastics and ninja staff while ensuring a safe, positive, and engaging environment for all participants. 
Models and promotes the YMCA’s mission of developing a healthy mind, body, and spirit through quality recreation programming. 
Trains, mentors, and provides feedback to instructors and coaches to ensure consistent instruction, safety practices, and participant engagement. 
Oversees daily class operations, including staff coverage, class quality, equipment use, and program expectations. 
Assists with the development, implementation, and evaluation of gymnastics and ninja curriculum, lesson plans, and program improvements. 
Uses good judgment, flexibility, creativity, and sensitivity when addressing staff, participant, and parent needs. 
Ensures staff follow YMCA policies, procedures, Code of Conduct standards, and appropriate behavior management practices. 
Communicates effectively with participants, parents, staff, and leadership to address questions, concerns, and program needs. 
Monitors class attendance, staff schedules, and program records to maintain accurate documentation. 
Maintains a clean, organized, and safe gymnastics/ninja environment while ensuring equipment and facility standards are met. 
Assists with staff scheduling, finding coverage, and communicating staffing needs with the Gymnastics Director. 
Supports hiring, onboarding, training, and ongoing development of gymnastics and ninja team members. 
Teaches gymnastics and ninja classes as needed, providing quality instruction, skill development, and a positive experience for participants. 
Ensures compliance with safety regulations, emergency procedures, and risk management practices; reports concerns to the Gymnastics Director and Risk Management as needed. 
Supports special events, competitions, camps, clinics, evaluations, and scholarship fundraising activities. 
Attends required trainings, meetings, and professional development opportunities as directed by Countryside YMCA and the Gymnastics Director. 
Performs other duties as assigned or required by business necessity.

Qualifications

REQUIRED SKILLS/ABILITIES :
Ability to demonstrate and teach a variety of gymnastics and ninja skills while ensuring proper progressions and safety practices. 
Reliable and punctual attendance with the ability to support daily program operations. 
Creative problem-solving skills with strong verbal and written communication abilities. 
Ability to supervise participants and staff with confidence, enthusiasm, and a focus on safety and positive experiences. 
Ability to provide leadership, guidance, and support to instructors while maintaining program quality. 
Must be at least 18 years of age and successfully complete a criminal background check.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: 

Ability to plan, lead, supervise, and participate in a variety of gymnastics and ninja activities in an indoor recreation setting. Noise levels will vary depending on participant activity and program operations within the gymnastics center. Role may require carrying, kneeling, pushing, pulling, sitting, climbing, lifting, running, stooping, crouching, standing, and walking. Must have the physical ability to assist participants, demonstrate skills when needed, and respond quickly to safety concerns or emergency situations.

REASONABLE ACCOMMODATIONS STATEMENT 

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.  Reasonable Accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
ABUSE PREVENTION STATEMENT: 

Countryside YMCA is committed to providing a safe environment for all children and vulnerable individuals in our care. We follow best practices for abuse prevention, including thorough screening, ongoing training, and clear behavioral expectations for staff and volunteers. We have a zero-tolerance policy for abuse and take all allegations and concerns very seriously. All employees are required to follow our child protection policies, complete required training, and report any suspicious or inappropriate behavior immediately.

new_jobs.description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.
At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.
Your Impact
Axon Community Connect enables public safety agencies to build voluntary, policy-based partnerships with businesses and community members. Through camera registration and secure camera integration, the program expands investigative reach and real-time situational awareness during critical incidents while maintaining privacy, transparency, and camera-owner control.
As the PSO Program Manager, Community Connect, you will lead the operational health and scalable execution of the Community Connect program across Axon’s U.S. customer base and growing international footprint.
You will establish the operating discipline that enables Program Coordinators to deliver consistent agency outcomes. This includes maintaining visibility into program performance, work-order health, delivery dependencies, technical readiness, and customer-impacting risks; strengthening the processes, tools, and playbooks used across the team; and ensuring complex issues receive the appropriate cross-functional attention.
You will serve as a program-level escalation resource, coordinating with Professional Services, Product, Engineering, Support, Sales, and Finance to remove blockers and drive resolution. You will also provide consultative support for hardware deployment readiness, remote hardware configuration and activation, connectivity, and camera integration requirements.
Your work will enable agencies to launch and sustain Community Connect programs that extend operational visibility, strengthen community participation, and scale responsibly without compromising privacy or the customer experience.
What You’ll Do
Location:
Remote - PT or MT Time Zones 
Travel:
Approximately 30%
Reports to:
Manager, Program Management (Community Connect)
Partner with PSO leadership to implement scalable workflows, operating rhythms, documentation, and reporting that support consistent program delivery.
Maintain visibility into overall program performance, project status, delivery milestones, dependencies, and customer-impacting risks.
Coordinate with Product, Engineering, Support, Sales, Finance, and other internal teams to remove delivery blockers, manage escalations, and improve the customer experience.
Support work-order management and closure activities, including quality checks, documentation, and internal handoffs.
Serve as a technical resource for deployment planning, hardware readiness, network connectivity, configuration, and integration requirements.
Support the deployment of Cores placed in the field by Community Connect team members, including remote configuration, activation, validation, and onsite technical support when needed.
Troubleshoot hardware, network, connectivity, and video-integration issues; document findings and coordinate escalation with the appropriate technical resources to drive resolution.
Create and maintain technical readiness guidance, deployment checklists, troubleshooting resources, and escalation paths for common Community Connect deployment scenarios.
Develop and maintain playbooks, training materials, job aids, and knowledge resources that enable consistent team execution.
Identify recurring delivery, technical, and process issues; partner with leadership to implement improvements that strengthen program execution at scale.

Project/Program Manager

KBR is seeking a Project/Program Manager to join our team in Albuquerque, NM supporting the Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center (AFNWC). An active DoD TS/SCI, SAP Eligible clearance is required.

Key Responsibilities

Assist planning, execution, and management of program cost, schedule, and performance for Nuclear Systems Integration Division’s branches (Tail Kit Assembly [TKA], Weapon Systems Integration and Test, Logistics, or Program Management) depending on background and experience.
Support AFNWC/NDS management of current and future air-delivered gravity bomb and warhead families (B83, B61-12 and -13, W80) including test variants and support equipment.
Support the Branch Chief and technical support teams to accomplish Branch tasks.
Support Government Team development, implementation, and control of contracts including acquisition strategy and planning.

Document strategic plans detailing senior leader policy and direction for Division programs.

Develop system requirements based on military capabilities and sustainment concepts.
Develop and maintain system specifications, traceability, and compliance through project lifecycles.
Determine resource requirements such as personnel, facilities, and budgets to facilitate program execution.
Maintain awareness of nuclear certification programs and processes.
Support DoDI 5000.02, DoDM 5030.55/AFI 63-103 and DOE Phase 6.X acquisition process and AFI 63-125 Nuclear Certification processes.
Plan, research, analyze and assess weapons systems acquisition in terms of development, production, and employment.
Formulate plans and make strategy recommendations to meet weapon system cost, schedule, and performance objectives.
Use multi-attribute tradespace exploration philosophies and workflows to ensure digital material management and multi-criteria decision making are implemented throughout the portfolio of programs, projects, and initiatives.

Qualifications

Exceptional written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
Superior collaboration and organizational skills.
Proactive and highly motivated.

Expertise in qualitative and quantitative analysis techniques for measuring the effectiveness, efficiency, and productivity of acquisition systems or services.
Expertise in Government project governance and stakeholder communication.

Understanding of the Nuclear Weapons Life Cycle and the Phase 6.x process for refurbishment activities of existing nuclear weapons systems (B61, B83, W80 integration into the Long Range Standoff Missile).
5 - 10 years of project management experience supporting National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA), DOE, AF Global Strike Command, or related organization.
Advanced STEM degree is preferred.
Acquisition Professional Development Program (APDP) certification preferred.
Familiarity with reliability and statistical software.

40hrs

Working Hours: Standard

new_jobs.description:
If you like solving complex international trade problems using your deep compliance skills, this is the opportunity for you! The Senior International Trade Compliance Analyst provides expert leadership in ensuring the company's adherence to U.S. and international trade regulations. This role involves strategic oversight of compliance initiatives, managing highly complex export/import authorizations, and acting as a senior advisor on compliance matters.

As SNC's corporate team, we provide the company and its business areas with strategic direction and business support spanning executive management, finance and accounting, operations, human resources, legal, IT, information security, facilities, marketing, and communications.

Responsibilities

Design, develop, and maintain compliance dashboards, reports, and metrics to identify trends, anomalies, risks, and drive actionable insights and improvements to leadership and stakeholders.
Develop and present key trade compliance program metrics and performance indicators to senior leadership on a recurring basis.
Build and maintain automated reporting tools to reduce manual effort and improve data accuracy and timeliness.
Translate complex regulatory and operational data into clear, concise visual reports for both technical and non-technical audiences.
Lead and support the integration of trade compliance tools and systems with internal ERP, logistics, and business platforms.
Collaborate with IT and business operations teams to design, test, and implement system enhancements that support compliance workflows.
Serve as a subject matter expert and provide ongoing technical support for international trade compliance tools and systems
Identify opportunities to leverage technology to streamline and automate compliance processes.
Document system integration workflows, data flows, and technical specifications to ensure international trade requirement integration, operational continuity, and auditability.
Plan, manage, and execute trade compliance projects from initiation through completion, ensuring deliverables are met on time and within scope.
Coordinate cross-functional teams including legal, logistics, engineering, security, and IT to drive compliance initiatives forward.
Develop project plans, timelines, risk registers, organizational change management (OCM) strategy, and status reports for compliance initiatives.
Serve as a liaison between compliance, business, and technology stakeholders to align priorities and communicate project progress.
Support and manage continuous improvement efforts within the trade compliance function.

Qualifications You Must Have

Bachelor’s degree in a related field (Business, Supply Chain, Data Analytics, Information Systems, International Trade, or similar).
5+ years of experience in international trade compliance, data analytics, or a related field.
Relevant experience can be considered as a substitute for the required educational qualifications. In the absence of a degree, a minimum of 9 years of related experience is required.
Higher level relevant degree may substitute for experience.
Demonstrated experience in data analytics, report building, or business intelligence tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau, Excel, SQL, or similar).
Experience with maximizing MS365 capabilities (Sharepoint, Powerapps, Powerautomate, Copilot, etc.)
Experience supporting or leading system integration projects or technology implementations.
Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
Experience working in multi-disciplinary, cross-functional teams.

Qualifications We Prefer

Experience in the Aerospace and Defense industry.
Certification in Trade Compliance, Project Management, or Data Analytics.
Advanced knowledge of trade compliance platforms such as OCR EASE, DECCS, SNAP-R, and ACE.
Experience with ERP systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle, Costpoint) and their integration with trade compliance workflows.
Working knowledge of ITAR, EAR, Foreign Trade Regulations (FTR), Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA), and other relevant trade regulations.
Proficiency in scripting or programming languages for data automation (e.g., Python, R, or similar).
Experience developing AI use cases and building agentic workflows.
Familiarity with Agile, Waterfall, or other structured project management methodologies.

Essential Functions

Ability to work on a computer for extended periods.
Requires good hand and finger dexterity for data entry.
Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing.
Must be able to travel up to 10% of the time.
Ability to work in an office or hybrid environment.

This posting will be open for application for a minimum of 5 days and may be extended based on business needs.

Estimated Starting Salary Range: $118,360.24 - $162,745.34. Compensation varies depending on a wide array of factors, such as candidates' key skills, relevant work experience, and education/training/certifications. The disclosed range estimate may be adjusted for any applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled.

SNC offers a generous benefit package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, 401(k) with 150% match up to 6%, life insurance, 3 weeks paid time off, tuition reimbursement, and more.

Important Notice

This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a Secret U.S. Security Clearance. U.S. Citizenship status is required as this position needs an active U.S. Security Clearance for employment. Non-U.S. citizens may not be eligible to obtain a security clearance. The Department of Defense Consolidated Adjudications Facility (DoD CAF), a federal government agency, handles the adjudicative aspects of the security clearance eligibility process for industry applicants. Adjudicative factors which affect the outcome of the eligibility determination include, but are not limited to, allegiance to the U.S., foreign influence, foreign preference, criminal conduct, security violations and illegal drug use.

new_jobs.description:
Pay Range:
Targeted salary of $10.00/hour, based on education and experience.

Benefits Eligible:
No

Work Schedule

Approximately 10–20 hours per week.
The supervisor will work with each student employee to establish a schedule that accommodates their class schedule.

Travel:
Not required

Position Introduction

The Dodge Family College of Arts and Sciences Dean's Office is seeking two undergraduate students to join its Data Analysis team as Student Data Analysts.

This position provides students with practical experience in data analysis, research, reporting, and data visualization. Student Data Analysts will work with institutional data and support projects that inform decision-making across the College. Students will receive hands-on training and regular guidance as they develop skills in Excel, Power BI, data validation, analytical reasoning, and professional communication.

We are especially interested in students who would like to remain in the position for multiple semesters, allowing them to continue developing their skills and take on increasingly independent work.

Responsibilities

Build and maintain reports, dashboards, charts, and analytical models using Excel and Power BI.
Retrieve, organize, review, and validate institutional data.
Assist with enrollment, student, academic program, and other College-level analyses.
Respond to data and reporting requests from departments and Dean's Office leadership.
Research and investigate unexpected trends or inconsistencies in data.
Learn to query databases and work with institutional data sources.
Document data sources, calculations, assumptions, and analytical methods.
Summarize findings in clear language for non-technical audiences.
Assist with longer-term analytical projects from initial research through final presentation.
Manage multiple assignments and deadlines.
Handle confidential student and personnel information in accordance with FERPA and University policies.
Perform other related duties as assigned.

Student analysts will learn to answer three important questions about their work:

How did you arrive at that number?
Where did the data come from?
How do we know it's right?

What You'll Learn

Develop advanced Excel and Power BI skills.
Learn how professional analysts approach and validate data.
Work with real-world datasets and business questions.
Improve analytical writing and data visualization skills.
Present findings to College leadership and departmental administrators.
Complete projects that can be discussed in future job or graduate school interviews.
Receive regular feedback and professional development from the Executive Director.

Students who demonstrate strong performance and increased proficiency may be considered for additional responsibilities and advancement opportunities, subject to University processes and available funding.

Students from all DFCAS majors are encouraged to apply. Advanced data-analysis experience is not required. We are looking for students who are curious, careful, willing to learn, and interested in understanding not only what the numbers show, but why. Students with at least two semesters remaining at OU are especially encouraged to apply.

Selection Process

We want to see how you like to solve problems. The interview includes a short data-analysis exercise: you'll build a simple chart and write a brief interpretation of the data, and then we'll talk through it together. We're evaluating analytical thinking, attention to detail, and communication — not advanced Excel skills, and not how you perform under pressure. If you need help with Excel, just ask.

Use Of AI

AI tools may be used as part of the application process, interview exercise, and position when appropriate.

Applicants should be prepared to explain how they used AI and how they reviewed or verified its output. AI is considered a tool to support analytical work, not a replacement for independent judgment.

All use of AI while working with University information must comply with applicable University requirements regarding confidentiality, FERPA, information security, and institutional data.

Required Education And Experience

Must be currently enrolled in the Fall Term as a student at the University of Oklahoma.

Hiring contingent upon verification of current student status.

Must be a student in the Dodge Family College of Arts and Sciences.

Skills

Basic familiarity with Microsoft Excel.
Strong written communication skills.
Attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
Ability to think critically and solve problems.
Ability to learn new software and analytical methods.
Ability to maintain confidentiality.
Ability to maintain a consistent weekly work schedule.

Department Preferences

Coursework or experience in one or more of the following areas is helpful but not required:

Statistics
Economics
Research methods
Data analysis
Quantitative reasoning
Computer science or programming
Business analytics
Social science research
Research and analytical writing

No
